That would then lead to new results for load response, which would lead to new prices, and so on, until an equilibrium is reached. 54 While this study represents an upper bound of load response, it does indicate that such significant system load impacts may be possible, particularly if large quantities of customer loads are operating with the same (or similar) dispatch algorithms, in response to the same (or similar) price signals. It will be important to consider potential impacts of non-marginal changes to load, and particularly the impacts of highly coordinated load response, as dynamic pricing and the associated automation technologies are rolled out. New methods for predicting price response, developing prices, and valuing the load impacts will be needed to best represent a figure with substantial price responsive loads. 4.2 Evaluation of tariff design scenarios This study assessed three designs for hourly dynamic prices. Across all scenarios, we assume the overall tariff design features a symmetric price for customers buying and selling electricity from the grid, and we assume that the dynamic tariff is fully volumetric, accounting for all utility costs/revenues required. The three designs differ in what portion of costs are allocated dynamically, i.e. varying on an hourly basis with system conditions, as opposed to being a fixed volumetric charge. In the Full tariff design, 100% of the costs are dynamic, while the Medium and Mild tariff have only 50% and 20% of the costs fluctuating, and 50% and 80% of costs constant, respectively. In comparing the prices from the three tariff scenarios, we find that the Full scenario exposes customers to the highest variation of prices, offering both the greatest opportunity for consumption of low-cost electricity and the greatest exposure to high prices. The Full scenario also offers the greatest opportunity for price savings, with daily price differentials (difference between average of 4 highest and lowest hours in each day) that are generally 30-50% larger than the Medium scenario. The Medium design offers significantly larger differentials than the Mild scenario, generally twice the savings potential. Table 10.
